factual_methodology.summary: UNDP publication dated 11 October 2026, IMF and WBG meeting calendars, BLS October release calendar and IBGE September IPCA. Modelled exposure distinguished from realised poverty.

novelty.summary: New UNDP assessment dated 11 October, not a rewrite of 10 October's market and Brazil inflation recap.

editorial_publication_readiness.summary: Continuous argument on fuel price transmission, fiscal protection, sovereign debt, and prospective institutional evidence. English and Brazilian Portuguese reviewed for parity.

visual_evidence_readiness.signature: 1 table + 2 same-unit bar charts + 1 causal flow + 1 geographic mechanism map in each locale
visual_evidence_readiness.summary: UNDP poverty threshold scenarios explicitly overlapping; fuel prices separate from poverty units; mechanisms qualified.

contrary_evidence: The UNDP figures are scenario estimates under full pass-through; actual poverty effects can be mitigated by income adjustments and protection policies.
Net energy exporters may gain export revenues even as domestic fuel costs increase.
New multilateral liquidity or lower energy prices could relieve fiscal stress.
limitations: No fresh Sunday financial-market settlement was claimed.
UNDP poverty estimates depend on conditional pass-through and overlap across alternative thresholds.
Country-sample averages are not population-weighted global inflation.
IMF and BLS releases scheduled for 13–15 October were not yet available at information cutoff.
notes: Evidence and translation consistency checked against primary-source pages; build CI and live-route verification required after publication.

en.title: Global Macro — fiscal protection narrows as energy and debt pressures converge before Bangkok
en.deck: A new UNDP assessment quantifies rising fuel costs, potential poverty exposure and shrinking fiscal room before the IMF–World Bank meetings in Bangkok.
en.regime: High energy costs and elevated debt service limit developing economies' room to shield households.
en.key_risk: Expensive fuel and debt servicing reduce the capacity to protect vulnerable households without displacing essential spending.
